 Home News Mirra Andreeva Jessica Pegula Leylah Fernandez surpasses Mirra Andreeva and Jessica Pegula and sets new 2026 WTA record after latest victory in Ningbo
 Max Kilham Wed 21 October 2026 20:00, UK Add to Preferred Sources Leylah Fernandez booked her spot in the Ningbo Open quarter-finals on Wednesday after defeating Aliaksandra Sasnovich in three sets. 
 Fernandez , a finalist at the 2021 US Open, triumphed 7-5, 6-7, 6-3 on Centre Court and will play Ekaterina Alexandrova in the quarter-finals.
 The Canadian is seeking to win her second WTA 500 event of the year after capturing the Singapore Open title in September .
 Fernandez has also been successful at WTA 500 events in previous years, winning the 2024 Eastbourne Open and the 2025 Washington Open .
 Fernandez’s success at the WTA 500-level has continued into this year, as evidenced by her latest statistical feat.
 Leylah Fernandez has been the most successful WTA 500 player of 2026 so far
 With victory against Sasnovich on Wednesday, Fernandez recorded her 15th WTA 500-level victory of the season.
 As per OptaAce, Fernandez now leads all other WTA players in this statistical area, overtaking Jessica Pegula and Mirra Andreeva – who both have 14 WTA 500-level victories this year – with her latest triumph.

 Stuttgart Open Alexandra Eala, Zeynep Sonmez 
 Strasbourg Open Leolia Jeanjean, Magdalena Frech 
 Bad Homburg Open Katie Boulter 
 Washington Open Magda Linette 
 Singapore Open Kyoka Okamura, Alycia Parks, Mirra Andreeva, Maja Chwalinska, Talia Gibson 
 Ningbo Open Elise Mertens, Aliaksandra Sasnovich 
 Leylah Fernandez’s 15 WTA 500 victories in 2026 [as of October 21] Fernandez can extend this record to 16 by beating Ekaterina Alexandrova on Friday.
 Fernandez has a 2-3 record against the Russian. However, the Canadian did emerge victorious from their last match at the 2026 Wuhan Open, winning 6-4, 3-6, 6-3 in the round of 64.
 More Tennis News The winner of Fernandez and Alexandrova will play either Marie Bouzkova or Sara Bejlek in the Ningbo Open semi-finals.
 Who is the defending Ningbo Open champion?
 Elena Rybakina, the new world number one, triumphed at the 2025 Ningbo Open.
 The Kazakhstani player, seeded third at last year’s event, defeated Dayana Yastremska, Alja Tomaljanovic, Jasmine Paolini and Ekaterina Alexandrova en route to the title.
